title: International Interests in Mobile Equipment (Cape Town Convention) (Consequential Amendments) Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would adjust aviation and personal property securities laws to support Australia's implementation of the Cape Town Convention and its aircraft protocol.

It would recognise qualifying Airservices Australia liens, enable aviation regulator functions for aircraft deregistration and export, and confirm the international framework's priority over inconsistent securities law.
Its substantive amendments would begin with the companion Act, while domestic personal property securities legislation would continue applying wherever there was no inconsistency.
changes: An Airservices statutory lien for unpaid charges would outrank an international security interest if the lien had been registered first.
The Civil Aviation Safety Authority could record, remove and act on irrevocable deregistration and export request authorisations.
The companion Convention Act would be added to the list of laws prevailing over inconsistent personal property securities provisions.
summary.affected: Aircraft creditors and debtors, Airservices Australia and the Civil Aviation Safety Authority are affected.

speeches.speaker: Anthony Albanese
speeches.brief: Briefly noted that the companion International Interests in Mobile Equipment (Cape Town Convention) (Consequential Amendments) Bill 2013 also has bipartisan support and would benefit the Australian aviation industry.
